newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rightist admits political killing-prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: German rightist admits political killing-prosecutor.

text.p: A 24-year-old right-wing extremist admitted on Wednesday that he had shot a Berlin book dealer to punish east German communists, prosecutors told a Berlin court on Wednesday.
They said the extremist said he had shot the book dealer because he was angry at the Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS) for disrupting a far-right rally in Berlin on February 15.
The PDS operates an office in the same building as the shopkeeper, who was seriously wounded.

The 24-year-old man is also accused of shooting dead one police officer and wounding a second during a routine traffic inspection on Sunday. He was captured after a chase and shootout with police on a motorway east of Hamburg.
Berlin's anti-extremist office for the protection of the constitution warned in a recent report that right-wing militants might resort to violence in the future.
It said that there had been an increase in explosives found among right-wing groups in Berlin in the last year, especially in the eastern sections.
The report estimated that there were more than 800 neo-Nazis in Berlin, of whom about 500 were militants.

It said far-right activities across Germany were being organised from Berlin. Hundreds of extremists from around the country regularly attend far-right meetings of the "Berlin Cultural Society of Prussia", a group that plays a key role in recruiting new members.
